d: What is the cosmic microwave background (CMB)? In this video, we explain the leftover radiation from the Big Bang in simple words — from how the Big Bang theory predicts an expanding universe (confirmed by Hubble's Law in the 1920s), to how Penzias and Wilson accidentally discovered the CMB in 1965 while working on a radio receiver. Learn why the early universe was opaque, how the first atoms formed 380,000 years after the Big Bang, and why NASA called the CMB "the first baby picture of the universe."
